title: Adaptive microflow anchoring for multi-panel dashboards and modal continuity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a density-aware layout system that preserves interaction continuity across dashboard multi-panel layouts, modals, and charts in a cross-browser-safe way. This ticket covers design prototypes, engineering handoff, and acceptance criteria for: panel anchoring during viewport changes, smooth modal stacking and focus restoration, chart canvas resizing fallbacks, and table virtualization behavior when panels collapse. Constraints: must work in Chrome, Firefox, Safari (Desktop + iOS), and Edge; avoid heavy runtime layout thrashing; rely on progressive enhancement where platform features (container queries) are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-panel dashboard anchors: when resizing width or toggling side panels, primary content panels maintain visual continuity (no layout jumps > 8px) and keyboard focus remains predictable.
Modal continuity: stacked modals preserve z-order, scroll locking does not break scroll restoration on Safari iOS, and ESC/back navigation closes top modal only.
Chart fallbacks: when canvas resizing hits performance constraints or CSS transforms cause blurring (Firefox), chart falls back to high-DPI SVG + simplified tooltips without layout regression.
Tables: virtualized table rows do not lose hover/selection state during progressive collapse/expand of sibling panels and maintain accessible row focus order.
Cross-browser parity: documented mitigations for Safari/Firefox quirks included in handoff and verified in manual QA with linked test matrix.
Performance: first meaningful paint for dashboard page at typical dataset (5 widgets, 2 charts, 1 table) stays within +10% of current baseline; no regressions on mobile CPU emulation.
decisions: Use CSS container queries where available for panel sizing; polyfill with ResizeObserver-based class toggles for older Safari/Firefox versions.
Prefer transform: translateY for microflow anchor animations to avoid layout reflow; use will-change sparingly and remove after animation completes.
Implement modal stack management in Console core (single source of truth) so both UI kit and legacy pages reuse same focus/scroll locking logic.

Charts: primary path uses Canvas rendered by charting library; if computed devicePixelRatio or forced transforms cause blurring, render an SVG fallback and mute heavy interactions (tooltip throttling).
Table virtualization: maintain a stable id-to-index mapping to preserve selection/hover states during DOM recycling; expose a small API to temporarily pin rows during animation windows.
open_questions: Should we expose a developer-facing API for 'anchor hints' so product teams can mark a widget as visually important across layout changes?
Is it acceptable to degrade chart interactions on older iOS to preserve visual fidelity, or do we need feature parity for interaction?
Can engineering allocate a small runtime budget for a ResizeObserver micro-batcher to smooth rapid panel toggles?
Do we want telemetry for layout-anchoring regressions (e.g., frequency of >8px jumps) included in console-telemetry?
activity_log: 2025-01-28: Ticket created by Maya Chen with initial research notes on Safari iOS scroll locking and Firefox subpixel canvas rendering issues.

2025-01-30: Low-fi prototypes posted. Noted that when collapsing left nav quickly, Chrome preserved focus but Safari moved focus to body — likely due to passive focus handling. Added prototype link to Figma.

2025-02-01: Design review — attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nambiar (Eng), Jonas Meyer (Frontend). Feedback: prefer transform-based micro-animations and explicit focus restoration. Priya raised concern about ResizeObserver performance under many widgets.
2025-02-02: Engineering spike assigned (ENG-47921) to benchmark ResizeObserver vs CSS-only approach. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4578 for early experiment (WIP).

2025-02-04: Cross-browser QA run (manual) on staging: Chrome/Edge stable passed; Firefox exhibited 0.5px canvas blurring on 2x zoom; Safari desktop fine but Safari iOS needed custom scroll locking workaround. Documented steps and screenshots in Confluence.
2025-02-05: Design updated prototypes to include 'anchor hint' microcopy and a compact fallback pattern for charts (SVG fallback state). Added acceptance criteria for performance budgets.
2025-02-06: PM review (Sharon Liu) — approved approach pending engineering perf benchmarks; asked to include telemetry plan and a rollout gating criterion. Added release tag console-2025.02.
Next steps: engineering to land ResizeObserver micro-batcher spike and chart fallback component (ENG followups). Schedule accessibility walkthrough with QA + Design.
